clue.text: Mild expletive concerning female in launch

parts.note: 'blast!' is a mild curse
of can mean about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone swears gently about a woman during a rocket launch.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment a rocket leaves the pad is its lift-off, the start of its flight.

clue.text: Vassal's legal right to bag game freely

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads as the noun

indicators.note: bagging means putting into a bag, so the jumble goes inside

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

indicators.note: loosely arranged, so the letters of game are rearranged

explanation.surface: A feudal servant's legal right to catch game without restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' is the anagram signal for game, and 'to bag' puts the result inside the legal right; a vassal was a lord's sworn man in feudal times.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal owed feudal service to a lord, being his sworn man.

clue.text: Lit up during brawl, producing, weapon

indicators.note: during the brawl means inside the word for brawl

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or brawl

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Someone drunk in a fight pulls out a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit up' looks like drunk, but 'up' is the reversal signal in this down clue, and 'during' puts the turned word inside the brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a narrow blade.

clue.text: Old-fashioned sports gear is better

parts.note: out means out of fashion
a strip is a team's sports kit

explanation.surface: Old-style sports kit turns out to be superior.
explanation.walkthrough: A STRIP is the British word for a team's matching sports kit.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to surpass or exceed, i.e. be superior to.

clue.text: In nostalgic memory of The Thunderer?

definitions.text: In nostalgic memory of The Thunderer?

parts.words: In nostalgic memory of The Thunderer?
parts.note: The Thunderer is the old nickname of The Times newspaper, so the phrase reads as being on behalf of that venerable paper

explanation.surface: A fond remembrance of a deity of thunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thunderer is a traditional nickname for The Times of London, the paper this puzzle appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in memory of past days, here punning on the newspaper's name.

clue.text: Opening line in theatre cut

explanation.surface: A first night when a line in a play is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is an operating theatre, and the line is the surgeon's cut, not an actor's speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical cut makes an opening in the body; the surgeon's line in an operating theatre is this.

clue.text: Plantation in Mexico had a nice new layout

indicators.note: arranging something with a new layout means its letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A Mexican estate has a pleasant redesigned layout.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish-speaking America a large estate or ranch is a hacienda.

clue.text: Tight-fisted painter consumed fish

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed, so the painter goes inside the mean word

parts.note: stingy means mean or tight-fisted
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: A miserly artist ate a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat fish with a venomous spine in its tail.

clue.text: Sort of mining project viewed by public

indicators.note: the project is seen by the public, so the word for public is placed in front

parts.note: open means accessible to the public
to cast is to project, as light or a shadow

explanation.surface: A mining venture is put on public display.
explanation.definitionFit: Surface mining from an open pit, rather than underground shafts, is this kind of mining.

clue.text: It roamed all over the place, as an agent for peace

indicators.note: scattered in every direction, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something wandered everywhere in its role as a peacemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between who brokers settlements in disputes is a peace agent.

clue.text: Disregard figure endlessly seen round civic centre

indicators.note: seen round means placed around the other piece, enclosing it
without its end, so the last letter of the shape word is cut off

parts.note: an oblong is a geometric figure, a rectangle

indicators.note: the centre of the word civic is its letters without the outer ones

explanation.surface: Someone ignores a statue seen going around the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' suggests a statue or number, but it is a geometric shape; 'endlessly' drops its last letter and 'centre' keeps civic minus its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is a state of being forgotten or disregarded entirely.

clue.text: We may put a figure on it (see foot of column)

definitions.text: We may put a figure on it (see foot of column)

parts.words: We may put a figure on it (see foot of column)
parts.note: reads like a note about writing a number down, but describes the base a statue stands on, also found at the foot of a column

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a number somewhere, with a footnote reference.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a figure as a number and a footnote, but the figure is a statue and the column is architectural.
explanation.definitionFit: The base supporting a statue or forming the bottom of a column is its plinth-like support.

clue.text: Condescend with hesitation to accept son as architect

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: to deign is to condescend
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone reluctantly lowers themselves, hesitating, to take on their son as architect.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect is a person who plans and draws up buildings, a planner.

clue.text: Not on the house? How insulting!:

explanation.surface: A drink not given free provokes an indignant cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Not on the house means not free, i.e. not complimentary; insulting remarks are disparaging.

clue.text: Hidden resentment indicated initially in working to rule

indicators.note: the initials are placed in the middle of the jumble
working suggests the letters are worked over into a new order
initially picks out the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Concealed grievance is shown at first in a go-slow by workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges TO RULE as ULTEOR; 'initially' gives RI, put 'in' it. Working to rule is a British form of industrial protest.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulterior motive is concealed or undisclosed.

clue.text: Commander scowled and became red in the face

parts.note: CO is commanding officer
loured means frowned or scowled

explanation.surface: An officer frowned and flushed with anger.
explanation.definitionFit: To colour up is to blush, flushing red.

clue.text: Stain on feathers leads to price reduction

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the stain comes first

parts.note: a mark is a stain
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: A mark on soft plumage results in a cheaper sale price.
explanation.definitionFit: A markdown is a cut in the price of goods.

clue.text: Meat I dropped, for example, outside office

indicators.note: outside means surrounding the other piece
dropped means left out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: venison is deer meat

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned meat, for instance outside the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' removes I from VENISON, leaving VENSON. 'office' looks like a workplace, but it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a daily church service; evensong is the evening one.

clue.text: It creates a stir where storminess is unjustified

definitions.text: It creates a stir where storminess is unjustified

parts.words: It creates a stir where storminess is unjustified
parts.note: stirring tea in a cup recalls the phrase storm in a teacup, a fuss over nothing

explanation.surface: Something causes a fuss when the outrage is unwarranted.
explanation.walkthrough: A storm in a teacup is a fuss over a trivial matter; the stirring utensil is what really disturbs a teacup.
explanation.definitionFit: The little implement used to stir tea literally makes a stir in a cup.

clue.text: Sharp old counsel first to explain new meaning

indicators.note: first means the old word for counsel is placed at the start

parts.note: rede is an archaic word for advice or counsel
fine means sharp, as a fine point

explanation.surface: A keen former lawyer is the first to clarify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counsel' suggests a barrister, but REDE is archaic for advice.
explanation.definitionFit: To redefine is to state the meaning of something anew.

clue.text: Put up with unusual role in gallery

indicators.note: the jumbled word is placed inside the gallery name

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery

indicators.note: out of the ordinary, so the letters of role are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor endures an odd part in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The TATE is a group of British art galleries, the best known in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with something is to bear or endure it.

clue.text: Suggestive of evil — but it's right for the viewer

explanation.surface: Something seems wicked, yet looks proper to whoever is watching.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry this term means the bearer's left side of a shield, which is on the right as the viewer sees it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister means ominous or menacing; heraldically it is the shield-bearer's left, which faces the onlooker's right.

clue.text: Game a little girl observed, 'subject to being admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the second piece goes inside the name

parts.note: Ros is a short form of the girl's name Rosalind or Rosamund
under means subject to, as in under orders

explanation.surface: A child watches a game, as long as she is allowed in.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUNDERS is a British bat-and-ball game rather like baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounders is a team bat-and-ball game played in British schools.

clue.text: Defence starts to go into action at end of a game

indicators.note: the initials are placed after the other pieces, at their end

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: the starts of the next words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A team's defence springs into action as the match ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence of one's opinions or conduct.

clue.text: Drive remorselessly across river defended by Chinese vessel

parts.note: over can mean across, as in over the road

indicators.note: defended means surrounded protectively, so the river letter sits inside the pan

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese cooking pan

explanation.surface: Someone drives relentlessly across a river guarded by a Chinese ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To overwork someone is to drive them too hard without mercy.

clue.text: Contrive to be train driver in US

explanation.surface: Someone schemes to become a locomotive driver in America.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer a result is to contrive it; in American usage the driver of a locomotive is so called.
